question: In 1992, this man was convicted of raping beauty pageant contestant Desiree Washington and served three years of his sentence in an Indiana prison. In February 1990, he suffered one of the biggest upsets in sports history when 42-to-1 underdog Buster Douglas knocked him out in the tenth round in Tokyo. At just 20 years old in November 1986, he knocked out Trevor Berbick to become the youngest heavyweight champion in boxing history. (*) In a June 1997 rematch billed as "The Bite Fight," he was disqualified for biting off part of Evander Holyfield's ear. For 10 points, name this boxer nicknamed "Iron Mike."

This man was knocked out with one second left in the sixth round of his fourth fight against Juan Manuel Marquez in December 2012, a bout later named Fight of the Year. In 2016, he was elected to the Senate of the Philippines after previously serving in its House of Representatives. This boxer forced Oscar De La Hoya to quit on his stool after the eighth round of their December 2008 bout. (*) In May 2015, he lost a unanimous decision to Floyd Mayweather Jr. in a bout billed as the "Fight of the Century." For 10 points, name this Filipino boxer nicknamed "Pacman," the only eight-division world champion in boxing history.

This boxer's promotional entourage and personal brand are known as "The Money Team," reflecting the nickname he adopted after starting his career as "Pretty Boy." He topped Forbes' list of the world's highest-paid athletes multiple times in the early-to-mid 2010s. In August 2017, he came out of retirement to face UFC star Conor McGregor in a boxing crossover bout, winning by tenth-round TKO to improve to 50 wins. (*) In May 2015, he defeated Manny Pacquiao by unanimous decision in a bout billed as the "Fight of the Century." For 10 points, name this boxer who retired with a perfect 50-0 professional record.

In February 2015, this athlete submitted Cat Zingano via armbar just 14 seconds into their UFC 184 title bout, the fastest finish in UFC title-fight history. She won a bronze medal in judo at the 2008 Beijing Olympics, becoming the first American woman to medal in Olympic judo. In November 2012, she became the first female fighter signed to the UFC and its inaugural women's bantamweight champion. (*) Her title reign ended in November 2015 when Holly Holm knocked her out with a head kick at UFC 193. For 10 points, name this MMA pioneer and WWE star known for her armbar submission.

At age ten in 1995, this driver introduced himself to Ron Dennis at an awards ceremony by saying "one day I'd like to race for your team," and McLaren signed him to its young driver program three years later. In his 2007 rookie season, this man stood on the podium in his very first Grand Prix in Australia and finished the year just one point behind Kimi Räikkönen. (*) This driver is recognized as the first Black driver in Formula One history and, unusually for a top F1 driver, has no widely used paddock nickname. In 2021, this man lost the World Championship to Max Verstappen on the final lap of the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix after a contentious late safety-car restart. For 10 points, name this British driver who holds Formula One's all-time records of 106 Grand Prix wins and a share of the record seven world titles.
answer: Lewis Hamilton [or Lewis Carl Davidson Hamilton]

question: This driver made his Formula One debut as a last-minute substitute for the jailed Bertrand Gachot at the 1991 Belgian Grand Prix, driving for Jordan and out-qualifying his veteran teammate Andrea de Cesaris. Because of his brilliant performances in wet conditions, he earned the nickname "Regenmeister," or rain master. At the 2006 Monaco Grand Prix, he parked his car at the Rascasse corner in an attempt to block Fernando Alonso from taking pole position. (*) In the 1997 season finale at Jerez, he attempted to ram Jacques Villeneuve off the track; he retired from the race and was later disqualified from the championship standings for the maneuver. For 10 points, name this German driver who clinched his first title by colliding with Damon Hill at the 1994 Australian Grand Prix and went on to win a joint-record seven World Championships with Benetton and Ferrari.

Before joining McLaren in 1988, this driver began his Formula One career with Toleman and Lotus. At the 1989 Japanese Grand Prix, he collided with his own teammate Alain Prost, then was disqualified for cutting through a chicane escape road to rejoin the race, handing Prost the championship despite this driver crossing the finish line first. (*) At the same circuit the following year, he deliberately rammed Prost, by then driving for Ferrari, at the first corner to clinch the title, an act he admitted a year later had been intentional. He won World Championships in 1988, 1990, and 1991, all with McLaren. For 10 points, name this Brazilian driver who was killed on May 1, 1994, when his car struck a concrete wall at the Tamburello corner during the San Marino Grand Prix at Imola, a day after Roland Ratzenberger died in qualifying.
answer: Ayrton Senna [or Ayrton Senna da Silva]

question: This driver was recommended to Hendrick Motorsports by Jeff Gordon after his previous team lost its sponsorship. Paired with crew chief Chad Knaus in the No. 48 car, he won the Daytona 500 in both 2006 and 2013, though Knaus was suspended by NASCAR and missed victory lane after the first of those wins. (*) In 2024, this driver was inducted into the NASCAR Hall of Fame. From 2006 through 2010, he won a record five consecutive NASCAR Cup Series championships. For 10 points, name this driver who tied Richard Petty and Dale Earnhardt's record of seven Cup Series titles, all won behind the wheel of Hendrick Motorsports' No. 48 car.

This golfer was inducted into the World Golf Hall of Fame in 1974, years before the end of his playing career. In 1962, this golfer defeated Arnold Palmer in a playoff at Oakmont Country Club to win the U.S. Open for his first professional victory, at age 22. At age 46, this golfer shot a final-round back-nine 30 to win the 1986 Masters, becoming that tournament's oldest champion and claiming a record sixth green jacket. (*) This golfer amassed 73 PGA Tour victories over his career, third all-time. For 10 points, name this golfer nicknamed the 'Golden Bear,' who holds the record for most men's major championships with 18.
answer: Jack Nicklaus [or Jack William Nicklaus; or the Golden Bear]
answerDisplay: Jack Nicklaus [or Jack William Nicklaus; or the Golden Bear]

question: Despite winning four other major titles, this golfer never captured the PGA Championship during his career. In 1967, this golfer became the first player to surpass $1 million in career PGA Tour earnings. At the 1960 U.S. Open, this golfer erased a seven-stroke deficit entering the final round, firing a front-nine 30 en route to a 65 that beat amateur Jack Nicklaus by two strokes at Cherry Hills. (*) A mix of iced tea and lemonade is named for this golfer, whose fans were nicknamed 'Arnie's Army.' For 10 points, name this golfer, known as 'The King,' who was the first man to win the Masters four times.
answer: Arnold Palmer [or Arnold Daniel Palmer; or the King]

question: In the second round of the 2001 Standard Register Ping, this golfer shot a 13-under-par 59, still the only sub-60 round in LPGA Tour history, and went on to win that event with a record score of 27-under. In 2003, this golfer accepted a sponsor exemption to play in the PGA Tour's Colonial tournament, becoming the first woman to compete in a men's PGA Tour event since Babe Didrikson Zaharias in 1945; she shot 71-74 and missed the cut by four strokes. (*) Later that year, this golfer completed a career Grand Slam by winning the LPGA Championship and the Women's British Open. This Swedish golfer won 72 LPGA Tour titles overall. For 10 points, name this golfer who retired with 10 major championships, one of the most dominant players in women's golf history.

At the 2017 Open Championship, this golfer hit his approach on the 13th hole so far right that he had to play his next shot from the driving range, taking an unplayable lie before making a bogey and sparking a five-under stretch over the final six holes to win at Royal Birkdale. The previous year, this golfer squandered a five-shot lead on the back nine of the Masters, hitting two balls into Rae's Creek for a quadruple-bogey seven at the par-3 12th hole. (*) In 2015, this golfer won the Masters wire-to-wire as a 21-year-old, tying Tiger Woods' 72-hole scoring record of 18-under 270. That same year, he also won the U.S. Open. For 10 points, name this golfer who needs only a PGA Championship victory to complete the career Grand Slam.

After losing a 1991 US Open quarterfinal to Jim Courier, this man's comment that he felt "relieved" the pressure to defend his title was gone drew criticism from Courier and Jimmy Connors. In a 1996 US Open quarterfinal against Alex Corretja, this man vomited on court during a fifth-set tiebreak but recovered to save a match point with a lunge volley and win. (*) This man never won the French Open, with a 1996 semifinal as his best showing there. He won his fifth and final US Open title by beating Andre Agassi in four sets in the 2002 final, the last match of his career. For 10 points, name this American nicknamed "Pistol Pete," who won a men's record 14 Grand Slam singles titles, including a record seven Wimbledon championships, before Roger Federer broke his mark.
answer: Pete Sampras [or Petros Sampras; or Pistol Pete]

question: This woman's father Peter was sentenced to 45 months in prison for tax evasion tied to her early earnings, a case that closed in 1997 only after she personally paid a 1.3-million-Deutsche-mark fine. A disturbed fan named Gunter Parche stabbed this woman's rival Monica Seles in 1993, later claiming he did it to help this woman reclaim the world No. 1 ranking. (*) At the 1988 French Open final, this woman demolished Natasha Zvereva 6-0, 6-0 in just 34 minutes, the most lopsided Grand Slam final of the Open Era. She capped a 1988 calendar-year sweep of all four majors by beating Gabriela Sabatini for Olympic gold in Seoul, completing tennis's first "Golden Slam." For 10 points, name this German woman, later married to Andre Agassi, who won 22 Grand Slam singles titles and remains the only player ever to win each major at least four times.

In his first major final, at the 1990 French Open, this man lost to Andres Gomez and later admitted he had been distracted by fear that his wig would fall off. In 1997, this man failed an ATP drug test for crystal methamphetamine and initially lied in a letter claiming a friend had spiked his drink, a fabrication he confessed to years later in his autobiography. (*) At the 1999 French Open final, this man rallied from two sets down to beat Andrei Medvedev in five sets, completing his career Grand Slam at age 29. He became the first male player to complete a career Golden Slam, having also won Olympic singles gold. For 10 points, name this American nicknamed "the Punisher" for his return of serve, who married Steffi Graf and won eight Grand Slam singles titles.

In August 2025, this player replaced coach Matt Daly with biomechanics specialist Gavin MacMillan, having previously worked with Brad Gilbert from mid-2023 to September 2024. At just 15 years old, this player upset five-time champion Venus Williams in straight sets during her Wimbledon main-draw debut in 2019, becoming the tournament's youngest qualifier ever. (*) In 2025, this player beat Aryna Sabalenka in a three-set French Open final, becoming the first American to win that title since Serena Williams in 2015. Two years earlier, she had also beaten Sabalenka for her first major title, at the 2023 US Open, becoming the first American teenager to win that tournament since Serena Williams in 1999. For 10 points, name this American player, born Cori Gauff, who reached a career-high ranking of No. 2.
answer: Coco Gauff [or Cori Dionne Gauff; prompt on "Coco"]
